rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: before capturing, count who attacks and who defends the piece. A piece that no other piece of its side defends is a hanging piece: taking it costs nothing.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.e2: This position comes from a game played on Lichess, and Black is to move. The white queen on e7 is hanging, and the white knight on e6 attacks the black queen on d8.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.p: Two black pieces reach the queen on e7. Find the best capture.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.certo: The queen captures the hanging queen and, at the same time, escapes the attack of the knight on e6. On e7 no white piece reaches it.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.revela: The right capture is with the queen: it takes the hanging queen and escapes the attack of the knight on e6. On e7 no white piece reaches it.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.err.c6e7.1: The knight captures the queen on e7, but the black queen is still on d8, within reach of the knight on e6.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.err.c6e7.2: With this move White has a resource: the knight on e6 captures the queen on d8, and White wins the queen back.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.err.c6e7.3: Back to the position: look for the capture that also takes the black queen out of the attack.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not capture the queen on e7. It is hanging: look for the capture.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the best capture on e7.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.l1: White has lost the queen and looks for material: the knight on e6 still attacks the rook on f8.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.l2: The knight captures the rook on f8, but there no white piece defends it: now the knight is the hanging piece.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.l3: The queen captures the knight on f8. Black has won the queen and the knight and given up only a rook.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex1.l4: In positions like this, with several captures at hand, count before you move: who attacks, who defends, and which of your pieces is left exposed after the capture.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: now the piece has a defender. The white rook on d7 is attacked by the rook on d3 and by the king on d8, and the rook on f7 defends it.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.e2: When both sides capture and recapture on the same square, there is an exchange. Before starting an exchange, count: here there are two attackers against one defender.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.p: Find the move that wins material on d7.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.certo: The rook captures on d7. If the rook on f7 recaptures, the king recaptures again, and Black ends the exchange a rook up.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is to capture on d7 with the rook: with two attackers against one defender, the last capture of the exchange belongs to Black.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.err.d8e8.1: On e8 the king attacks both white rooks, but each one defends the other.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.err.d8e8.2: With this move White has a resource: the rook on d7 gives check on e7, defended by the rook on f7, and the king must move.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.err.d8e8.3: Back to the position: count who attacks and who defends the rook on d7.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not win material on d7. Count who attacks and who defends the rook on d7.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: look for the capture on d7.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.l1: Now the king defends the black rook on d7, and the exchange does not pay for White. So they give check with the other rook.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.l2: The rook goes to f8 and checks the king on d8 along the eighth rank.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.l3: The king steps out of check to c7 and defends the rook on c8. Black is now a rook up.
rot.hangingPiece.ideia.ex2.l4: In positions like this, with pieces of equal value in the exchange, more attackers than defenders leave the last capture to you. Before counting, check the value of each piece.
rot.hangingPiece.demos.mutua.1: Attack: Black again. The white bishop on b3 is hanging, and the knight on c5 reaches it. But once the knight leaves, the black rook on a7 stands on the diagonal of the bishop on d4.
rot.hangingPiece.demos.mutua.2: The knight captures the hanging bishop on b3 and, from there, attacks the rook on c1, which is also undefended.
rot.hangingPiece.demos.mutua.3: White answers by capturing the hanging rook on a7, which stood on the diagonal of the bishop on d4 once the knight left c5.
rot.hangingPiece.demos.mutua.4: The knight captures the rook on c1. Adding up the captures, each side took a rook, and Black is left a piece up.
rot.hangingPiece.demos.troca.1: Attack: the white bishop on c6 is hanging, and the pawn on b7 reaches it. Before capturing, see what changes on the b-file.
rot.hangingPiece.demos.troca.2: The pawn captures the bishop. With the pawn gone from b7, the rooks face each other on the b-file.
rot.hangingPiece.demos.troca.3: The rooks attack each other along the b-file, and White starts the exchange: the rook captures the one on b8 with check.
rot.hangingPiece.demos.troca.4: The knight recaptures on b8. The exchange of rooks did not change the count, and the bishop Black won is still extra.
rot.hangingPiece.demos.excecao.1: Attack: Black again. The pawn on e4 attacks the queen on f5, and it has to move. The pawn looks hanging: is it worth capturing?
rot.hangingPiece.demos.excecao.2: The queen captures the pawn on e4.
rot.hangingPiece.demos.excecao.3: But the pawn on f3 recaptures. The queen is worth far more than a pawn: here the capture gives up the queen.
rot.hangingPiece.demos.excecao.4: Back to the position: the pawn on e4 had two defenders, the pawn on f3 and the queen on d5. A defended pawn is not a hanging piece.
rot.hangingPiece.demos.excecao.5: In an exchange, count the value too: capturing a defended piece with a more valuable piece usually costs material; with a less valuable piece, the exchange can pay. Here, the hanging piece is the knight on f4.
rot.hangingPiece.demos.excecao.6: The queen captures the hanging knight on f4 and, with the same move, escapes the attack of the pawn on e4.
rot.hangingPiece.pratica.valeAqui.enunci: Now with White. The black bishop on d1 and the pawn on a7 are hanging, but so is your knight on c6: the queen and the pawn on b7 attack it. Is a capture worth it? Play as White and find the best move.
rot.hangingPiece.pratica.valeAqui.fim: On e7 the knight captured the hanging bishop with check and attacked the queen on d5. The king stepped out of check, and the knight captured the queen.
rot.hangingPiece.pratica.valeAqui.err.c6: The knight escapes the attack and captures the rook on d8, but it is defended, the bishop on d1 escapes by capturing the pawn on c2, and the black queen stays on the board. Look for a capture that also attacks another piece.
The pawn was hanging, but it is worth little, and on a7 the knight has no safe square to go to. Look for a capture that wins more.
rot.hangingPiece.pratica.valeAqui.err.f1: The bishop was hanging, but so was your knight on c6: the black queen captures it. Look for a capture that takes the knight out of the attack.
rot.hangingPiece.pratica.valeAqui.err.a1: The bishop was hanging, but so was your knight on c6: the black queen captures it. Look for a capture that takes the knight out of the attack.
rot.hangingPiece.pratica.contagem.enunci: White again. Count who attacks and who defends each black piece, and what each one is worth. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.hangingPiece.pratica.contagem.fim: On d8 the bishop captured a rook defended only by the knight on c6. If the knight recaptures, the exchange will have given a bishop for a rook.
rot.hangingPiece.pratica.contagem.err.c4: The bishop captures the pawn on f7 with check, but the king recaptures: the exchange gives a bishop for a pawn. Look for a capture that leaves a profit.
rot.hangingPiece.pratica.contagem.err.d1: The rook captures the bishop on d4, but it has two defenders, the knight on c6 and the rook on d8: the exchange gives a rook for a bishop. Look for a capture that leaves a profit.
rot.hangingPiece.pratica.trocaDamas.enun: Stay with White. Before capturing, count the defenders of each black piece within reach of your queen. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.hangingPiece.pratica.trocaDamas.fim: On c3 the queen captured the hanging bishop with check. The black queen stepped in the way, also with check, and you accepted the exchange of queens: the bishop is still extra.
The queen captures the pawn on f5, but it has three defenders: the black queen recaptures, and you give up the queen for a pawn. Look for a black piece with no defender.
The bishop attacks the pawn on f5, but it has three defenders, and Black answers by attacking your bishop with the pawn from c5. Look for a black piece with no defender.
The bishop attacks the queen on d5, but it moves away, and you win no material. Look for a black piece with no defender.
